Ura Kidane Mehret
Ura Kidane Mehret
is a
round church
[
1
]
of the
Ethiopian Orthodox Church
, located on the
Zege peninsula
around
Lake Tana
in
Ethiopia
. It is part of the complex of the Convent of Mercy. At least one author considers it the most attractive church in the Lake Tana region.
[
2
]
The Ura Kidane Mehret
convent
was founded in the 14th century by the saint Betre Mariyam (
Amharic
"Rod of Mary"), although the present
circular church
dates from the 16th century.
[
2
]
Its interior is decorated with numerous murals painted between 100 and 250 years ago
[
when?
]
; subjects include
Negus
Tekle Haymanot of Gojjam
and his followers. The most significant were painted by
Alaqa
Engida during the reign of Emperor
Menelik II
. The church has its treasury in a nearby outbuilding, which contains the richly embroidered robes of
Negus
Tekle Haymanot and his wife
Laqetch Gegre Mehdin
, as well as the crowns of Emperor
Yohannes IV
, Emperor
Tewodros II
,
Negus
Tekle Haymanot, and Emperor
Tekle Giyorgis
.
[
3
]
